decision_reason: NASA Langley's current software catalog identifies CFL3D (LAR-16003-1) as an open-source structured-grid RANS solver and directly distributes this repository. The repo exposes the solver source and an Apache-2.0 license; the first grant-bearing code snapshot is the 2017-07-10 import. NASA's CFL3D site provides its user manual. Repository source has been quiet since 2022, so the status is Maintained only on the strength of the current NASA product page's direct distribution of this same source.

government_provenance.note: NASA Langley's LAR-16003-1 product page describes the exact CFL3D solver, labels the release Open Source, and its Download Now link resolves to the reviewed nasa/CFL3D repository.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE grants Apache License 2.0. The grant-bearing repository snapshot is https://github.com/nasa/CFL3D/commit/485dffbc8573ec7356f3d26fc282ac10c416ae33 (2017-07-10); it contains the software source as well as the license.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's CFL3D v6.4 user manual documents the exact solver and its use; the current NASA Software Catalog page provides the matching source distribution. README documentation points users to the NASA CFL3D documentation site.

decision_reason: The repository is a small NASA Goddard cFS application library, not a standalone flight-software product. Its README says it supplies functions to several cFS apps and claims NASA Open Source Agreement coverage, but the repo has no exact grant text or versioned license file; its four-commit history and 2017 release do not establish a current use/distribution path for this exact library. Hold pending an exact grant-bearing release/license and current cFS documentation or deployment tying this source to the supported framework.

government_provenance.note: The first-party README identifies the code as the NASA core Flight System Application Library and says the cFS framework was developed by NASA Goddard; NASA's current cFS page independently identifies the framework as NASA-origin software. This is a repository-specific project statement, not organization membership alone.

decision_reason: NASA Glenn's 2021/2022 EDS workshop presentation documents this exact Python ground-station GUI being built and demonstrated for the Regenerative Fuel Cell project; the repository contains source, a user manual, setup guidance, and Apache-2.0 terms. However, the repository's last source activity was November 2021, more than 48 months ago, and no current exact-product deployment, support, or distribution was found. Hold rather than infer current use from historic project evidence.

decision_reason: NASA Glenn's current Software Catalog identifies the Channel Emulator as open-source network-testing software and directly links this exact repository. NASA's Network Emulation Laboratory paper documents the named tool's operational use. Although repository changes stopped in 2016, the current NASA page continues official direct distribution of the same source, which meets the baseline's maintained-by-distribution exception; do not label it Active.

decision_reason: This repository is the former NASA EOSDIS CMR Catalogue Service for the Web application; its README documents the exact web service, Apache-2.0 app license, dependencies and setup. NASA's current endpoint page announces that CMR CSW has been retired, and GitHub records the repository archived on 2022-06-03. The code's historical implementation/use of OGC CSW is clear, but no current service exists and evidence that this retired app merits an exceptional Archived catalog record is unresolved. Hold pending an explicit historical-significance/product-family decision.
